we have combined the data from the Daya Bay, MINOS+, and Bugey experiments, and have excluded the LSND and the MiniBooNE allowed regions at 99% C.L. for Δm_{42}^{2}≤1.6  eV2.
we have combined searches for electron antine neutrino, muon antine neutrino and muon neutrino disappearance driven by mixing with sterile neutrinos.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new type of high-performance, low-cost, and high-efficiency, large-area, position-sensitive, and radiation-tolerant detector based on a new type of silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) technology.
neutrino oscillation phenomena, in particular, neutrino mixing and mass.
the study of the neutrino mixing angle θ_{μe}. This angle is a measure of the probability that an electron neutrino will be detected as a muon neutrino.

the global data set constrains sterile-neutrino oscillations below the sensitivity of existing reactor experiments, with exclusion power extending up to a mass splitting of Δm_{41}=6  eV, where the LSND and MINOS+ anomalies overlap.
